<details>

🌐 Web query:

`In Next.js App Router (v15+ / v16), what is the expected type shape for `searchParams` values in `page.tsx` (string vs string[] vs undefined), and recommended normalization pattern for query params like `token`?`

💡 Result:

Expected `searchParams` value shape in Next.js App Router (v15+ / v16) page.tsx: 1) `searchParams` prop itself is optional and is a Promise you must await. - The official page convention docs show `searchParams` typed as `Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>` and described as “A promise that resolves to an object” of the current URL’s search parameters. [1] 2) For each key in that resolved object, the value is one of: - `string` (common case: single query param) - `string[]` (when the URL contains the same key multiple times, e.g. `?token=a&token=b`) - `undefined` (when the key is absent) This union (`string | string[] | undefined`) is explicitly shown in the official type example. [1] Recommended normalization pattern (e.g. `token`): Because the type can be `string`, `string[]`, or `undefined`, normalize in two steps: - Await the promise to get the plain object. - Coerce the specific param to a single string (or leave undefined) by: - If it’s an array, pick the first entry (or join—your choice, but be consistent). - If it’s a string, use it. - If it’s undefined, set a default or keep undefined. Example pattern for `token` in `app/.../page.tsx` (Server Component): const searchParams = await props.searchParams; const tokenRaw = searchParams?.token; const token = Array.isArray(tokenRaw)? tokenRaw: tokenRaw; This aligns with the documented `string | string[] | undefined` shape and “await the promise” requirement. [1] Practical note: in the same docs, Next.js emphasizes `searchParams` is a request-time API and is not a `URLSearchParams` instance, so you should normalize from the provided object rather than expecting `.get()`. [1]

Citations:

- 1: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page

+  searchParams: Promise<{ token?: string | string[] }>;

-  const token = params.token;
+  const rawToken = params.token;
+  const token = typeof rawToken === 'string' ? rawToken : rawToken?.[0];

+  if (!token?.trim()) {
